header.running_head: The Enthusiasm of the Sahabah (RA) to Die and Give their Lives in the path of Allaah

blocks.text: Hadhrat Thaabit (RA) and Hadhrat Saalim (RA) Dig Holes During a Battle to Keep them from Fleeing and to Ensure that they are Martyred

The daughter of Hadhrat Thaabit bin Qais bin Shammaas (RA) narrates that when Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) requested the Muslim to fight against those who forsook Islaam from Yamaamah and the followers of Musaylama, Hadhrat Thaabit bin Qais bin Shammaas (RA) was amongst those who marched. When the Muslim army clashed with Musaylama and the Banu Haneefa tribe, the Muslims were defeated in three battles. It was then that Hadhrat Thaabit bin Qais bin Shammaas (RA) and Hadhrat Saalim the freed slave of Hadhrat Abu Hudhayfa (RA) said, "This was not how we fought during the time of Rasulullaah ﷺ." They then dug a foxhole for themselves, got in and fought until they were both martyred.[^1]

Hadhrat Muhammad bin Thaabit bin Qais bin Shammaas (RA) narrates that when the Muslims were initially defeated during the Battle of Yamaamah, Hadhrat Saalim the freed slave of Hadhrat Abu Hudhayfa (RA) said, "This was not how we fought during the time of Rasulullaah ﷺ." He then dug a foxhole for himself and stood in it. Carrying the flag of the Muhaajireen with him, he then fought until he was martyred. May Allaah shower His mercy on him. This occurred during the Battle of Yamaamah during the Khilaafah of Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) in 12 A.H.[^2]
blocks.narrator: Hadhrat Muhammad bin Thaabit bin Qais bin Shammaas (RA)

blocks.text: The Call Hadhrat Abbaad bin Bishr (RA) Made to the Ansaar Before he was Martyred

Hadhrat Abu Sa'eed Khudri (RA) reports that Hadhrat Abbaad bin Bishr (RA) said to him, "O Abu Sa'eed! Last night I saw (in a dream) that the sky opened up for me and then shut behind me (after I had entered). Inshaa Allaah, this indicates martyrdom." Hadhrat Abu Sa'eed Khudri (RA) says, "I told him that he had seen an excellent dream. During the Battle of Yamaamah, I then saw him calling to the Ansaar, 'Break the sheaths of your swords and separate from the others. Let us Ansaar separate! Let us Ansaar separate (from the other soldiers so that we may show our courage and encourage the others thereby)!' Four hundred soldiers only from the Ansaar gathered aside. Abbaad bin Bishr (RA), Abu Dujaanah (RA) and Baraa bin Maalik (RA) led them to the orchard (where the enemy had fortified themselves) and fought very hard. Abbaad bin Bishr (RA) was martyred. May Allaah shower His mercies on him. I saw so many wounds on his face that I could recognise him only by signs on his body."[^3]

Tabraani. Haythami (Vol.9 Pg.322) has commented on the chain of narrators. Ibn Abdul Birr has also reported the narration in Isti'aab (Vol.1 Pg.194), as has Baghawi, as quoted in Isaaba (Vol.1 Pg.196).
